entry.title: Cap Ferret Ocean Beach
entry.summary: Wild Atlantic beaches and high dunes at the tip of the Cap Ferret peninsula, facing the Banc dArguin. Swimming is best at the supervised beaches, since waves and rips are strong.

entry.title: Plage d'Argent
entry.summary: A long, silvery-white beach on Porquerolles, the largest of the Iles dHyeres, within a national park and without cars. Pine forest and warm clear water make it feel like the tropics.

entry.title: Hossegor Lake Beach
entry.summary: A calm sandy beach on the lake of Hossegor, ringed by pines and villas, offering a gentler alternative to the surf on the nearby ocean beaches. It has lifeguards in summer and is good for small children.

entry.title: Lacanau Ocean Beach
entry.summary: A broad sandy Atlantic beach backed by dunes and pines, with strong waves that have made Lacanau one of France best-known surf spots. The central beach is lively, and the southern sections are quieter.

entry.title: Zaton Beach
entry.summary: A long, shallow beach between Zadar and Nin on the Adriatic, mostly sand with pebbles in places. A flat shoreline and warm water make it popular with families.

entry.title: Makarska Beach
entry.summary: The long pebble and sand town beach of Makarska, with the dramatic Biokovo mountain wall behind it and a Mediterranean promenade along the back. Pine shade, water sports and cafes make it easy to spend a whole day.

entry.title: Punta Rata Beach
entry.summary: A long arc of small white pebbles under pine trees in Brela, with clear turquoise water and a rock off the shore. It is regularly named among the best beaches in Croatia.

entry.title: Praia da Zambujeira do Mar
entry.summary: A pretty cove in the Alentejo with a golden beach, dark cliffs and a lively little village on top. The Atlantic waves attract surfers, and the sea is cooler than in the Algarve.

entry.title: Praia da Ilha do Pessegueiro
entry.summary: A sheltered sandy beach on the Alentejo coast looking out at Pessegueiro Island and its small fort. The cliffs and wild coast around it are part of the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park.

entry.title: Praia dos Tres Irmaos
entry.summary: A sandy beach in Alvor, in the western Algarve, with golden sandstone cliffs and rock stacks that form little arches and caves at low tide. The high viewpoint above is as popular as the sand.

entry.title: Praia da Foz do Arelho
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach on the Silver Coast where the calm Obidos lagoon meets the open Atlantic, so you can pick between gentle lagoon water and ocean waves. Cliffs, dunes and fishing boats frame the view.

entry.title: Playa de Bolnuevo
entry.summary: A wide golden beach in Murcia with calm warm water, next to the Gredas de Bolnuevo, sandstone towers sculpted by wind and water. A beach that is quiet for its size.

entry.title: Playa de El Puntal
entry.summary: A small golden beach on the right bank of the Villaviciosa estuary in Asturias, with views across to the Rodiles dunes and a calm, semi-urban feel. It is easy to reach and good for gentle swimming.

entry.title: Cala d'Hort
entry.summary: A small, beautifully framed cove in south-west Ibiza where the dramatic rock of Es Vedra rises from the sea just offshore. Fish restaurants line the back of the beach and it is famous for its sunsets.

entry.title: Playa de Ris
entry.summary: A broad golden beach in Noja, Cantabria, with a long gentle shore, good swimming and dunes and green hills behind. Lifeguards watch the sea in summer.

entry.title: Playa de las Catedrales
entry.summary: A Galician coast of towering cliffs carved by the Atlantic into giant arches and caves, walkable only when the tide goes out. It is one of Spain most photographed natural monuments.

entry.title: Budoni Beach
entry.summary: A long sweep of fine white sand and clear shallow water on Sardinia north-east coast, backed by dunes and juniper. Part is free and part is equipped, which makes it easy for families.

entry.title: Torre dell'Orso Beach
entry.summary: A wide crescent of pale sand and shallow turquoise water in Salento, guarded by a watchtower and the famous Two Sisters rock stacks. Clear water and gentle depths make it a favourite for families.

entry.title: Cala Sinzias
entry.summary: A wide, gently shelving bay of fine pale sand and shallow turquoise water in south-east Sardinia, with granite rocks and pines on both sides. It suits families who want calm swimming close to Villasimius.

entry.title: Fetovaia Beach
entry.summary: A curved bay of golden sand and granite grains on Elba south-west coast, with calm clear water and a pine-scented hillside behind. It is one of the island most popular family beaches.

entry.title: Sansone Beach
entry.summary: A small bay of bright white pebbles and clear turquoise water on Elba north coast near Portoferraio. A short, steep path down through the hillside keeps it from feeling like a roadside beach.

entry.title: Mylos Beach
entry.summary: A wild, mostly pebbly beach south of Agios Nikitas, framed by steep green hills and bright blue water. A forest path or a short boat ride keeps it feeling remote.

entry.title: Kalamaki Beach
entry.summary: A long stretch of golden sand on Laganas Bay and part of the protected loggerhead nesting area. Wooden markers show where nests lie, and the beach is quiet in the evenings by design.

entry.title: Dafnoudi Beach
entry.summary: A small, sheltered pebble cove on the north tip of Kefalonia near Fiskardo, with calm turquoise water and a pine forest behind it. A rocky trail through the trees keeps the crowds small.

entry.title: Gidaki Beach
entry.summary: A remote pebble cove on the east coast of Ithaca, backed by pale cliffs and clear blue water. There is no road to the sand, which keeps it quiet compared with most Ionian beaches.

entry.title: Omaha Beach
entry.summary: A long, flat, sandy shoreline in Normandy, best known as one of the D-Day landing beaches of 1944. Memorials and the American cemetery above the beach make a visit both a quiet seaside walk and a place of reflection.

entry.title: Plage des Grands Sables
entry.summary: A long sandy beach on the east coast of the island of Groix, famous as one of the few convex beaches in Europe. The shape is created by opposing currents and slowly shifts over time, and the water is clear.

entry.title: Plage de la Cote des Basques
entry.summary: A long sandy beach beneath tall cliffs on the south side of Biarritz, known for surfing and for its dramatic sunsets. At high tide the sand disappears, so tide times matter here.

entry.title: Plage de Roccapina
entry.summary: A wide sandy bay in south-west Corsica, watched over by the Genoese tower and the granite Lion of Roccapina. Access is by a bumpy dirt track, and there are no services, so the beach stays quiet and wild.

entry.title: Sveti Jakov Beach
entry.summary: A small pebble and shingle cove east of Dubrovnik old town, with clear, deep blue water and wooded cliffs behind. It is calmer than the beaches nearest the walls, and the view of the coast is lovely.
